questions.sectionTitleEn: 16. Order of Precedence — (i) Official Warrant of Precedence
questions.sectionTitleHi: 16. वरीयता अनुक्रम (Order of Precedence) — (i) भारत का आधिकारिक वरीयता अनुक्रम
questions.topicTag: Indian Polity: 16. Order of Precedence — (i) Official Warrant of Precedence
questions.questionTextEn: Chiefs of Staff holding the rank of full General or equivalent rank. 1. Consider the following functionaries : 1. Cabinet Secretary 2. Chief Election Commissioner 3. Union Cabinet Minister 4. Chief Justice of India Their correct sequence in the Order of Precedence is :
questions.questionTextHi: पूर्ण जनरल या समकक्ष रैंक का पद धारण करने वाले चीफ ऑफ स्टाफ। 1. निम्नलिखित पदाधिकारियों पर विचार करें: 1. कैबिनेट सचिव 2. मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त 3. केंद्रीय कैबिनेट मंत्री 4. भारत के मुख्य न्यायाधीश वरीयता क्रम में उनका सही क्रम है:
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (C). The correct sequence in the order of precedence of the given functionaries is Chief Justice of India, Union Cabinet Ministers, Chief Election Commissioner, Cabinet Secretary. 2. In the order of precedure of the government of India which of the following come/comes above the Chief Justice of India? (a) Attorney General of India (b) Former President (c) Chief of Staffs (d) Speaker of Lok Sabha R.A.S./R.T.S.(Pre) 1997 Ans. (b) The order of precedence, are as follows- (1) President, (2) Vice-President, (3) Prime Minister, (4) Governors of the State, (5) Former Presidents, (5A) - Deputy Prime Minister, (6) The Chief Justice of India and the Speaker of Lok Sabha are equal in the table of precedence of Government of India. 3. As per Indian Protocol, who among the following ranks highest in the order of precedence? (a) Deputy Prime Minister (b) Former President (c) Governor of a State within his State (d) Speaker of Lok Sabha I.A.S. (Pre) 2003 Ans. (c) See the explanation of above question. 4. Who is the topmost civilian ofﬁ cer in Government of India? (a) Home Secretary (b) Defence Secretary (c) Cabinet Secretary (d) Lt. Governor of Delhi M.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 1998 Ans. (c) The Cabinet Secretary is the topmost civilian ofﬁ cer in the Government of India. The Cabinet Secretary is the ex-ofﬁ cio head of Civil Services Board, Cabinet Secretariat, Indian Administrative Service (IAS) and head of all Civil Services under the Rules of Business of the Government of India. 5. Who is the Highest Ranking Civilian Officer in Government of India? (a) Lt. Governor of Delhi (b) Defence Secretary of India (c) Cabinet Secretary of India (d) Principal Secretary to Prime Minister of India Chhattisgarh P.C.S. (Pre) 2003 Ans. (c) See the explanation of above question. 6. In the Indian Order of Precedence, who amongst the following comes ﬁ rst? (a) The Chairman of UPSC (b) The Chief Election Commissioner (c) The Comptroller and Auditor General (d) The Chief Justice of High Court (e) None of the above/More than one of the above 65th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2019 Ans. (e) Order of Precedence of the list is given below : 1. The chairman of UPSC- 9A 2. Chief Election Commissioner - 9A 3. Comptroller and Auditor General - 9A 4. The Chief Justice of High Court - 14 So, the correct answer will be (e). The Parliament (1) *Parliament is the legislative organ of the Union Government. *Article 79 to 122 in part V of the Indian Constitution deals with the Parliament. *According to Article 79, the Parliament of India consists of the President and the two houses - House of the people and Council of States. *Loksabha is also known as the "House of people". *Its maximum strength is 550. At present, it has 543 (States-524, UTs-19) members. *Out of 550 members, 530 members are representative of states, 20 members are representative of Union territories. If, in the opinion of the President, there is not enough representation of the Anglo-Indian Community in the Lok Sabha, then he could nominate two members of that community in the Lok Sabha. In this regard, the arrangements related to the Anglo-Indian Community have not been extended beyond the stipulated date (25 January, 2020) by 'The Constitution (One Hundred and Fourth Amendment) Act, 2019' [The Constitution (One Hundred and Twenty-Sixth Amendment) Bill, 2019]. Thus, the arrangements of nomination of two members of the Anglo- Indian community in the Lok Sabha has ended. *The allocation of statewise seat in the Lok sabha is based on the Census of 1971. *According to 84th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2001, the next assessment shall be held by the year 2026. *In Lok sabha states are allotted seats on the basis of population. *The normal tenure of Lok sabha, is 5 years from the date of its ﬁ rst meeting after the general elections but it can be dissolved by the President in between. *Under the Article 352, Loksabha can be extended during the time of National Emergency for one year at a time. *In any case of extension it can't continue beyond the period of 6 months after the emergency has ceased to operate. *The qualiﬁ cation of a person in order to be elected a member of Lok sabha are (a) He must be a citizen of India and (b) He must not be less than 25 years. (c) He must make and subscribe to an oath (d) He must possess other qualiﬁ cations prescribed by the Parliament.
